name: Linocut Press
tagline: Every round is a hand-pulled relief print: black ink, a vermilion plate that never quite lines up, and a Wolf stamped down where it lied.

fonts.ui: Archivo Extra Condensed 900 (wood-type numerals) + Caveat (pencil edition marks)

motifs: Two-plate printing: a red plate slightly misregistered under black type
Type is inked on paper and carved out of the black slab
Villagers are 16 two-ink carved stamps hung on a drying line with pegs
Printer's furniture: registration marks, tacks, deckled sheets, pencil edition notes
Brayer streaks and gouge marks as texture, never as decoration on top
reveal: The real answer gets a black owl seal and a 'The real Maya' stamp, then the red Wolf block slams down over the fake (press-and-squash motion, ink spatter, slip jolts) and 'It was the Wolf!' is stamped beneath it, with the answer text knocked out so it stays readable.
why: The host screen is mostly a carved black slab with one bright sheet of paper, so it glows without blinding a dim room, and the code is set in 262px condensed wood type that reads from across it. Two inks keep every screen instantly parseable at distance: black means the village, red means the Wolf.
images: art/stamp-*.png (16 two-ink stamps cut from stamps-sheet.png)
